events.description: HTS-led forces oust Bashar al-Assad; Jolani becomes de facto ruler and courts Western engagement.
Taliban congratulate Jolani on taking power in Syria.
Khalil ur-Rahman Haqqani dies; Gulbuddin Hekmatyar attends the funeral.
New York Times article 'How America Created the Enemy It Most Feared' published on Dec 12, updated Dec 17, profiling Mullah Osman in Nuristan.
New York Times article claims Taliban have all but cleared Afghanistan of poppy and illicit drugs.
Mullah Yaqoub travels to Turkey and is photographed with Afghan military officers at a weapons exposition.
New York Times puff piece on Sirajuddin Haqqani as the great moderate hope.
Hekmatyar appears in a video (aired by Al Jazeera) swearing allegiance to al-Qaeda.
Asaib Ahl al-Haq kidnaps five American soldiers at a provincial reconstruction center in southern Iraq, tries to take them to Iran, and executes them when pursued (date not stated by hosts).
US releases Qais and Laith al-Khazali and hundreds of AAH fighters as part of reconciliation while withdrawing (date not stated).
Pompeo says Taliban deal would see them defeat al-Qaeda, negotiate with Afghan government, and respect women's rights.

key_claims: Jolani led al-Qaeda's Syrian branch, reported to Baghdadi, and his dispute with Baghdadi, resolved by Zawahiri in Jolani's favor, produced the Islamic State.
HTS remains US-designated and is not seen as having changed; Western outreach is called naive wishful thinking.
The Taliban's issuing of national ID cards to foreign fighters is a playbook Jolani copies by making foreigners citizens.
Sirajuddin Haqqani is a US-designated terrorist with a $10M bounty and al-Qaeda ties, yet is portrayed as a moderate by Western analysts such as Barnett Rubin.
Hekmatyar attended Khalil Haqqani's funeral and allegedly pledged allegiance to al-Qaeda c.2006-07, never renounced.
The Khazali brothers were released by the US and returned to lead Asaib Ahl al-Haq, the most dangerous Iraqi special group.
Mullah Yaqoub, Taliban defense minister and Mullah Omar's son, visited a weapons expo in Turkey in late Nov 2024.
The NYT's Nuristan profile ignores al-Qaeda use of Kunar/Nuristan as rat lines, and its drug-eradication story uncritically accepts Taliban claims.
